current.text: Dejounte Murray, Trey Murphy, Zion Williamson and likely Yves Missi start for the Pelicans. The last starting spot is between Fears and Herb Jones.
A Pelicans beat reporter thinks Fears will start over Herb Jones. Reporting also says Joe Dumars wants him in the lineup.
Dejounte Murray is the starting point guard, so Fears does not have the lead guard role.
Experts expect a full season of Murray to limit Fears.
The Pelicans have a crowded rotation: Murray, Murphy, Herb Jones, Zion, Derik Queen and Missi, with Bennedict Mathurin added to the bench. This creates a minutes crunch.
Josh gives Fears at least a 50/50 chance to start over Herb Jones and is moving him up his rankings. He would draft Fears only if he starts. Value is outside the top 115 everywhere.
Fears is a handcuff to Dejounte Murray. If Murray is hurt or traded, Fears could give top 70 numbers.
Experts treat him as a late upside flyer for assists. In mocks he went around pick 104 and in round 11. He would be worth more with 30+ minutes.
One expert ranks him tier 8 among point guards and calls him badly underdrafted if he lasts to round 13.

durable.text: He is a dynamic, downhill lead guard. He keeps attacking the rim even when he is not scoring there, and he contributes across categories.
He does not shoot threes well enough to play off the ball as a two guard. He is slightly undersized and struggles on defense.

note: Both sites price him at about 1 USD. He ranks 168 on Yahoo and 129 on ESPN, so he sits near the bottom of our 144-player pool and could go undrafted. His projected line is broad with no category outlier: steals are his best (z +1.0) and FG% (43.2%) and turnovers are his weak spots, so he is a 1 to 2 USD bench flyer for any build that needs guard steals and assists. In the first weeks, check whether he beats Herb Jones for the starting spot and gets close to 30 minutes, and watch Dejounte Murray's health, which is what unlocks his upside.
